newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria oil flow station vandals unknown.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria oil flow station vandals unknown.

text.p: Unknown persons have vandalised a flow station abandoned during ethnic clashes in midwestern Nigeria in May, an oil executive said on Friday.
An official of the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, which owns the Warri River flow station told reporters that 80 percent of the facility had been destroyed.
A spokesman for Shell in Lagos said that the flow station had a nominal capacity of 30,000 barrels per day of crude oil.
"We don't yet know the reason for the vandalisation nor the culprits," he added.
The facility was built in 1971 and is one of 36 flow stations Shell has scattered in Warri area, its western zone operational centre in Nigeria.
Shell abandoned the station during clashes between armed youths of the Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes over the relocation of the Warri south local government council headquarters.
The Shell official said the damage was discovered when company staff went to the scene to check reports of oil spillage but found there was no leakage.
"Shell will have to conduct a proper study of the flow station to ascertain the worth and extent of the damage," said the official.
Shell frequently suffers from attacks by restive Nigerian oil communities angry that oil income is not being used to develop their oil-producing areas.
Before its closure, Warri river flow station was producing just 2,000 bpd.
